fixes.explanation: Right, baker. Judas (not Iscariot) asks, “Lord, why are You going to reveal Yourself to us and not to the world?” (John 14:22) Jesus has just said He will reveal Himself to the one who loves Him. Then Jesus replies to Judas in the very next verse. That's a question worth asking.

I see why you'd go there, because the word "way" does come up in this conversation. Thomas asks, “…how can we know the way?” (John 14:5) But in verse 2 Jesus says He is going to prepare a place for them. Same conversation, different word.
Not quite, friend. Philip says, “Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us.” (John 14:8) The word he uses is “us.” A sign for the world isn't in his words.

Close, friend, but Philip doesn't mention the others. He says, “Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us.” (John 14:8) The word he uses is “us.” Proof for the others isn't in his words.

That's it, baker. Jesus asks, “How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’?” (John 14:9) Just before that, He says that anyone who has seen Him has seen the Father. So He answers Philip's request with a question about Philip's own words.

Ooh, I see why you paused, friend, but it's TRUE! Jesus says, “…or at least believe on account of the works themselves.” (John 14:11) He gives them a second reason to believe. If My word isn't landing yet, He says, look at the works. I read that verse twice myself, so no shame here.

Sabbath is a good Bible word, friend, but it isn't in this verse. Jesus says, “If anyone loves Me, he will keep My word.” (John 14:23) Then He says the Father and He will make Their home with that person. The Sabbath doesn't show up in this answer.

Yes, baker. Jesus says the Advocate “…will teach you all things and will remind you of everything I have told you.” (John 14:26) Teaching and reminding, both coming from the Holy Spirit. I walk into the pantry and forget why every single time, so a promise like that sounds wonderful to me.

Yes, baker. Jesus says, “If you loved Me, you would rejoice that I am going to the Father…” (John 14:28) That's the word that fills the blank. He gives the reason too: “…because the Father is greater than I.”
That fits the mood of the night, friend. But Jesus says, “If you loved Me, you would rejoice that I am going to the Father…” (John 14:28) The word is “rejoice.” Weeping isn't in His words.
